metadata.title: Breed-Specific Dog Nutrition Knowledge Base
metadata.description: Structured diet guidance for ML-based canine diet recommendation system

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Measure kibble precisely; Labs are notorious overeaters and free-feeding must be avoided.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–90 minutes daily; includes fetch, swimming, and leash walks.
diets.Notes: Labs have a genetic mutation (POMC gene) that impairs satiety signaling, making strict portion control essential for weight maintenance.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce daily calorie intake by 20–25%; split into 3 smaller meals to reduce hunger.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90–120 minutes daily; low-impact options like swimming preferred to protect joints.
diets.Notes: Obese Labs are at high risk for hip dysplasia and diabetes. A veterinarian-supervised calorie-restricted diet with high protein preserves lean muscle mass during weight loss.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Gradually increase daily caloric intake by 10–15%; monitor weight weekly.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes daily; include muscle-building activities like hill walks.
diets.Notes: Underweight Labs may have parasites or metabolic issues; always rule out medical causes before increasing caloric intake.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use large-breed puppy formula; avoid overfeeding to prevent accelerated bone growth.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–40 minutes daily; avoid high-impact jumping until 18 months to protect growth plates.
diets.Notes: Lab puppies must receive large-breed puppy food, not small-breed or standard puppy formulas, to ensure controlled mineral ratios that prevent developmental orthopedic disease.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce caloric intake by 10–20% compared to adult; add joint supplements.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; gentle walks and swimming, avoid strenuous activity.
diets.Notes: Senior Labs (7+ years) are prone to obesity, arthritis, and kidney disease. High-quality protein maintains muscle mass while reduced fat and phosphorus support organ health.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed twice daily to reduce bloat risk; avoid exercise 1 hour before and after meals.

Recommended_Foods: Large-breed adult kibble with real meat first ingredient
diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–120 minutes daily; mental stimulation and physical tasks are equally important.
diets.Notes: German Shepherds have sensitive digestive systems and a predisposition to exocrine pancreatic insufficiency; high-quality, easily digestible protein sources are essential.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Cut portions by 15–20%; use a measuring cup and track intake weekly.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes daily; structured activities like agility or schutzhund training.
diets.Notes: GSDs rarely become obese but may gain weight after spaying/neutering; high-protein low-fat diets preserve muscle during caloric restriction.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add calorie-dense foods gradually; increase daily ration by 10% per week until target weight.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–75 minutes; incorporate muscle-building resistance activities.
diets.Notes: Working or highly active GSDs may lose weight due to high energy expenditure; performance formulas with 30%+ protein and 20%+ fat are appropriate.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed large-breed puppy food; divide daily ration into 4 equal meals until 6 months old.

Foods_to_Avoid: Raw meat (risk of pathogens in puppies)
diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes twice daily; avoid high-impact running until 18 months.
diets.Notes: GSD puppies are prone to panosteitis (growing pains); balanced calcium-to-phosphorus ratios in puppy food reduce orthopedic risk.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Transition to senior formula at age 7; reduce total calories by 15%.

Recommended_Foods: Senior large-breed kibble with joint support
diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; gentle structured walks, avoid prolonged strenuous exercise.
diets.Notes: Senior GSDs are prone to degenerative myelopathy and hip dysplasia; omega-3 rich foods and joint supplements significantly improve mobility and quality of life.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Measure all portions; Goldens will eat past satiety if allowed.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–90 minutes daily; fetch, swimming, hiking.
diets.Notes: Goldens are among the most cancer-prone breeds; antioxidant-rich foods (berries, leafy greens) and omega-3 fatty acids may offer some protective benefits.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use a slow feeder bowl; divide daily ration into 3 small meals to manage hunger.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes daily; low-impact swimming is ideal.
diets.Notes: Overweight Goldens face elevated cancer and joint disease risk; weight reduction to BCS 4-5/9 should be the primary goal with vet oversight.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add calorie-dense toppers to regular meals; increase by 10% weekly.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60 minutes daily; moderate activity while building weight.
diets.Notes: Underweight Goldens should be evaluated for parasites or GI disease before a gain protocol is started.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Do not free-feed; use large-breed puppy formula strictly.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes twice daily; no high-impact until 12–18 months.
diets.Notes: Golden puppies on large-breed formula develop bones more slowly and correctly, reducing adult joint disease risk.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Transition to senior formula at 8 years; add omega-3 and antioxidant supplements.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; gentle walks and light swimming.
diets.Notes: Antioxidant-rich senior diets may help reduce oxidative stress linked to the breed's high cancer prevalence.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use a slow feeder bowl; Bulldogs eat fast and are prone to gas and bloat.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes daily; avoid exercise in heat due to brachycephalic airway.
diets.Notes: Bulldogs have short snouts (brachycephalic) making breathing during exercise difficult; diet must prevent obesity to reduce respiratory strain.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce daily caloric intake by 20%; split into 3 meals to reduce begging and gorging.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily; only in cool weather, use cooling vests in heat.
diets.Notes: Obese Bulldogs face severe respiratory distress; weight loss is often medically urgent and should be vet-supervised.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Increase ration by small amounts; Bulldogs with skin folds may develop dermatitis if overfed fat.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily in cool conditions.
diets.Notes: Gaining weight in Bulldogs must be balanced carefully due to respiratory constraints; consult vet before any gain protocol.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed medium-breed puppy kibble in small portions; watch for gas and digestive upset.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15–20 minutes twice daily; short low-intensity play sessions.
diets.Notes: Bulldog puppies often have sensitive stomachs; limited ingredient diets reduce allergy and GI upset risk.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Senior Bulldogs need reduced calories; monitor weight monthly.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15–20 minutes daily in cool conditions; monitor breathing closely.
diets.Notes: Aging Bulldogs often develop cardiac and respiratory issues; a lean body condition is the single most important dietary goal.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Consistent portion sizes; Poodles are sensitive to dietary changes.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes daily; swimming, agility, and fetch.
diets.Notes: Standard Poodles are athletic and intelligent; high-quality protein supports both muscle maintenance and cognitive health.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce daily calories by 15%; substitute low-calorie vegetables for part of kibble.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–75 minutes daily; active play and agility training.
diets.Notes: Poodles rarely become obese but post-neuter weight gain is common; high-protein reduced-calorie diet preserves lean muscle.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add nutrient-dense toppers; increase daily intake by 10% weekly.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45 minutes daily; moderate activity during weight gain phase.
diets.Notes: Underweight Poodles may have GI malabsorption; high-quality digestible protein with added fat calories is effective.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed medium-breed puppy kibble; transition to adult food at 12 months.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes twice daily; socialization walks and play.
diets.Notes: Standard Poodle puppies develop rapidly; DHA supplementation supports neural development in this intelligent breed.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Switch to senior formula at 7–8 years; add antioxidant and joint supplements.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–40 minutes daily; swimming and gentle walks.
diets.Notes: Senior Standard Poodles are prone to Addison's disease and bloat; small, consistent meals and stress-free feeding routines are important.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed multiple small meals to prevent hypoglycemia; use a precise measuring spoon.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily; indoor play and short walks.
diets.Notes: Chihuahuas have very high metabolic rates; calorie-dense small-breed food prevents hypoglycemia while frequent meals maintain stable blood sugar.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Even tiny excess calories cause weight gain in Chihuahuas; reduce daily ration by only 10–15%.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily; indoor play encouraged.
diets.Notes: Even 0.1kg overweight is significant for a 2kg dog; calorie reduction must be minimal and gradual to avoid hypoglycemia.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Increase meal frequency rather than size; add nutrient-dense toppers to kibble.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15–20 minutes daily; light indoor play.
diets.Notes: Underweight Chihuahuas can deteriorate rapidly; high-frequency feeding with calorie-dense food is essential.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed every 3–4 hours to prevent hypoglycemia in very young puppies.

Recommended_Foods: Warm puppy milk replacer (if under 8 weeks)
diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 10–15 minutes play sessions; puppy socialization activities.
diets.Notes: Chihuahua puppies are extremely vulnerable to hypoglycemia; feeding schedules and emergency glucose gel should always be on hand.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Transition to senior small-breed formula at age 8–10; watch for dental disease affecting eating.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15–20 minutes daily; gentle indoor walks.
diets.Notes: Senior Chihuahuas commonly develop dental disease and cardiac issues; soft or moistened food helps with dental pain while low-fat supports heart health.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Beagles will steal and overeat; secure all food and measure portions with a scale.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60 minutes daily; nose-work and sniff activities ideal.
diets.Notes: Beagles are scent-driven and food-motivated; puzzle feeders slow eating, improve satiety, and provide mental stimulation.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Cut calories by 20%; use a slow feeder and food puzzles to extend meal times.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 75–90 minutes daily; scent trails and brisk walks.
diets.Notes: Beagles are one of the most obesity-prone breeds; even small treats add significant calories relative to their body size.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Increase daily intake gradually; add protein-rich toppers.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes daily.
diets.Notes: Underweight Beagles should be evaluated for parasites; deworming before starting a gain protocol is recommended.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use small-medium breed puppy kibble; avoid free-feeding to establish portion habits early.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes twice daily; puppy play and socialization.
diets.Notes: Establish strict feeding routines in Beagle puppies early; their food-obsessive nature develops young and controlled portions from puppyhood prevent adult obesity.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce total calories by 10–15%; senior Beagles are particularly prone to obesity.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; nose-work activities remain excellent for senior enrichment.
diets.Notes: Senior Beagles are at risk for hypothyroidism and obesity; regular thyroid screening alongside dietary management is recommended.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Maintain strict portions; even small weight gain severely stresses the spine.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; flat walks, avoid stairs and jumping.
diets.Notes: Dachshunds have elongated spines highly vulnerable to intervertebral disc disease (IVDD); maintaining an ideal lean body weight is critical to spinal health.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce caloric intake by 20%; green beans can substitute up to 25% of kibble to add volume.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes daily on flat terrain; swimming is excellent low-impact exercise.
diets.Notes: Weight loss in Dachshunds is medically urgent as back problems are severely worsened by obesity; target BCS 4/9 under vet supervision.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Increase by small amounts; avoid overfeeding fat as this worsens spinal risk.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes on flat ground.
diets.Notes: Weight gain in Dachshunds should be carefully monitored; even target weight must remain within the healthy range to protect the spine.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use small-breed puppy kibble; never free-feed as obesity habits form early.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15–20 minutes; gentle play, avoid jumping or stairs.
diets.Notes: Dachshund puppies must be prevented from jumping from furniture early; weight management habits established in puppyhood protect long-term spinal health.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce calories by 10–15%; soft food may be needed if dental issues are present.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20 minutes daily; flat gentle walks only.
diets.Notes: Senior Dachshunds frequently develop IVDD and back paralysis; strict weight control and low-impact activity are the most effective dietary and lifestyle interventions.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed from a raised bowl to reduce bloat risk; avoid exercise 1 hour around meals.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–90 minutes daily; high-energy play, running, agility.
diets.Notes: Boxers are energetic and muscular; high-quality protein supports muscle maintenance. They are brachycephalic and prone to bloat, so feeding management is critical.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce portion by 15–20%; maintain exercise levels to preserve muscle.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes daily; active structured exercise.
diets.Notes: Weight gain in Boxers often occurs post-neutering; maintaining high exercise with caloric reduction is effective.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use performance kibble and add protein-rich toppers gradually.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60 minutes daily; muscle-building activities.
diets.Notes: Very active Boxers may need performance-level nutrition to maintain healthy body weight.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed large-breed puppy formula; transition to adult food at 12–18 months.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes twice daily; play in safe areas.
diets.Notes: Boxer puppies grow rapidly and require large-breed puppy formulas to prevent orthopedic developmental issues.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Transition to senior formula at 7 years; add cardiac and joint supplements.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; avoid heat.
diets.Notes: Boxers have a high incidence of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and cancer; taurine-containing diets and antioxidant-rich foods are important in senior years.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Tiny kibble designed for toy breeds; feed precisely measured small amounts.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily; indoor play and short outdoor walks.
diets.Notes: Pomeranians have high metabolic rates; calorie-dense small-breed food prevents hypoglycemia while portion control prevents obesity.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Even 50g excess weight matters on a 2kg dog; reduce by 10–12% only.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–25 minutes daily.
diets.Notes: Small caloric reductions have proportionally large effects in toy breeds; frequent vet weight checks are recommended during weight loss.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add tiny amounts of high-calorie toppers; monitor closely.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15 minutes daily; light indoor activity.
diets.Notes: Very low body weight in Pomeranians is an emergency; veterinary assessment before starting a gain protocol is essential.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Every 3–4 hours; hypoglycemia risk is very high in Pomeranian puppies.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: Short 10-minute play sessions; gentle handling.
diets.Notes: Pomeranian puppies are at extreme hypoglycemia risk; emergency glucose gel should always be available and feeding must never be skipped.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Soft or moistened kibble; dental disease common in senior Pomeranians affects eating.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15–20 minutes daily; gentle indoor activity.
diets.Notes: Senior Pomeranians commonly develop tracheal collapse and dental disease; soft foods and maintaining lean weight reduce tracheal strain.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Huskies self-regulate well; still measure portions to prevent excess.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90–120 minutes daily; running, sledding, hiking.
diets.Notes: Huskies evolved to run long distances on low-calorie intake; they are efficient metabolizers and can thrive on moderate portions of high-fat, high-protein food.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce by 10–15%; Huskies rarely need significant weight loss.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 120 minutes daily; increased running or trail exercise.
diets.Notes: Husky weight gain usually indicates insufficient exercise rather than overeating; dramatically increasing exercise is often the primary intervention.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Increase fat and protein; Huskies in heavy work need performance-level nutrition.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–90 minutes; structured endurance training.
diets.Notes: Working or sled Huskies require significantly more calories; fat is the preferred energy source for this breed.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use medium-breed puppy kibble; avoid large-breed formulas (too low in calories for rapid growth).

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–40 minutes; playtime and short leash walks.
diets.Notes: Husky puppies should be fed consistently; their self-regulation instinct develops early but structured mealtimes build healthy habits.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Transition to senior formula at 8–9 years; maintain lean weight.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes daily; moderate paced walks and light running.
diets.Notes: Senior Huskies remain active longer than many breeds; maintaining high-quality protein prevents muscle wasting in their naturally lean frames.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use toy-breed kibble; measure portions carefully as small breed caloric needs are precise.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes daily; indoor play and short walks.
diets.Notes: Shih Tzus have sensitive skin and are prone to food allergies; limited ingredient diets reduce dermatitis and GI upset.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce daily ration by 10–15%; substitute cucumber or carrot for part of kibble.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily; gentle walks.
diets.Notes: Shih Tzus are brachycephalic; obesity worsens breathing difficulties, making weight loss a health priority.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add small amounts of nutrient-dense toppers to each meal.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20 minutes daily; gentle activity.
diets.Notes: Weight gain in Shih Tzus may indicate dental disease preventing proper eating; dental evaluation is recommended before dietary intervention.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use toy-breed puppy kibble; frequent small meals prevent hypoglycemia.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15 minutes twice daily; gentle play.
diets.Notes: Shih Tzu puppies have low hypoglycemia tolerance; do not skip meals and keep emergency glucose gel accessible.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Soft or soaked kibble for dental-compromised seniors; reduce calories by 10%.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15–20 minutes daily; very gentle activity.
diets.Notes: Senior Shih Tzus are prone to kidney disease and dental problems; low-phosphorus diets and soft food are important in late-stage senior care.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed from a raised bowl to reduce GDV (bloat) risk; no exercise within 1 hour of meals.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–90 minutes daily; structured exercise and obedience work.
diets.Notes: Rottweilers require high protein to maintain substantial muscle mass; joint support supplements are recommended from middle age.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce portions by 15–20%; maintain protein to preserve substantial muscle.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes daily; structured walks and swim sessions.
diets.Notes: Overweight Rottweilers face severe joint problems; weight loss protects hip and elbow dysplasia-prone joints.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use performance or working breed kibble; add protein-rich toppers gradually.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60 minutes daily; resistance activities.
diets.Notes: Rottweilers can lose muscle quickly when ill; high-protein diets are essential during recovery and weight restoration.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use large-breed puppy formula; avoid overfeeding to prevent accelerated bone growth.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–40 minutes; avoid high-impact activity until 18 months.
diets.Notes: Rottweiler puppies are highly susceptible to developmental orthopedic disease; large-breed puppy food with balanced Ca:P ratios is non-negotiable.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Transition to senior formula at 7 years; add joint and cardiac supplements.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; gentle walks and light swimming.
diets.Notes: Senior Rottweilers are prone to osteosarcoma (bone cancer) and joint disease; lean weight, anti-inflammatory omega-3s, and antioxidant foods are prioritized.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Measure daily portions carefully; Cockers are prone to obesity and pancreatitis.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes daily; walks, fetch, and water activities.
diets.Notes: Cocker Spaniels are prone to pancreatitis; a strictly low-fat diet is essential and high-fat foods must always be avoided.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce by 20% and use a slow feeder; very strict low-fat diet.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60 minutes daily; brisk walking and light swimming.
diets.Notes: Weight loss in Cocker Spaniels must use a very low-fat diet due to pancreatitis risk; even treats must be zero-fat vegetables.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Increase calories via protein and complex carbs rather than fat due to pancreatitis risk.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45 minutes daily; gentle activity during weight gain.
diets.Notes: Weight gain in Cocker Spaniels must be via lean protein and carbs only; fat-based calorie increases risk pancreatitis attacks.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use medium-breed puppy kibble; moderate fat content only.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes twice daily; gentle play and socialization.
diets.Notes: Cocker Spaniel puppies inherit pancreatitis predisposition; selecting a puppy kibble with moderate fat (~12–15%) is important from day one.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Transition to senior formula at 8 years; strictly maintain low-fat to protect aging pancreas.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes daily; gentle walks.
diets.Notes: Senior Cockers commonly develop pancreatitis, liver disease, and hypothyroidism; a low-fat, high-antioxidant senior diet addresses multiple age-related risks.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Active Border Collies need adequate calories; adjust portion based on daily activity level.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90–120 minutes daily; herding, agility, and frisbee.
diets.Notes: Border Collies are extremely active and intelligent; they need high protein and adequate fat to fuel their exceptional energy demands.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce portions by 10–15%; increase exercise first as Collies rarely gain weight from food alone.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 120 minutes daily; increased structured exercise.
diets.Notes: An overweight Border Collie almost always indicates insufficient exercise rather than overfeeding; activity increase should precede dietary restriction.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Switch to working dog or performance kibble; add protein-rich toppers.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes; maintain activity level during weight gain.
diets.Notes: Working Border Collies may lose weight rapidly during intensive work periods; performance nutrition is essential.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use medium-breed puppy formula; transition to adult at 12 months.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes twice daily; mental stimulation activities alongside physical play.
diets.Notes: Border Collie puppies need both physical and mental stimulation from early on; nutrition must support rapid brain and body development.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Senior Collies remain active longer; maintain higher calorie intake than other senior dogs until activity clearly declines.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes daily; mentally engaging activities remain important.
diets.Notes: Senior Border Collies are prone to degenerative myelopathy and cognitive decline; DHA and omega-3 rich diets support both neurological and joint health.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: No exercise 1 hour before or after meals; Dobermans are highly susceptible to GDV (bloat).

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–90 minutes daily; structured obedience and agility work.
diets.Notes: Dobermans are genetically predisposed to dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and von Willebrand disease; taurine and L-carnitine supplementation alongside grain-inclusive diets is strongly recommended.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce by 15%; maintain protein to preserve lean muscle mass.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes daily; structured high-energy exercise.
diets.Notes: Weight gain in Dobermans often accompanies reduced exercise; caloric restriction should be paired with restored exercise routine.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Increase portion size gradually with 3 smaller meals to reduce bloat risk.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60 minutes daily; avoid immediately post-meal.
diets.Notes: Maintaining grain-inclusive food even during weight gain is critical for Dobermans due to cardiac risk.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Large-breed puppy food only; do not use small-breed formulas.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes twice daily; avoid high-impact exercise until 18 months.
diets.Notes: Doberman puppies must be on grain-inclusive large-breed puppy food from day one; grain-free diets are contraindicated due to breed-specific cardiac risk.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Senior formula with cardiac support; add taurine and L-carnitine supplements.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; gentle structured walks.
diets.Notes: DCM management in senior Dobermans requires grain-inclusive food, taurine, and L-carnitine; regular cardiac monitoring is essential alongside dietary management.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use a slow feeder; Frenchies gulp food which worsens gas and GI issues.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes in cool temperatures; never in heat.
diets.Notes: French Bulldogs are extremely brachycephalic; obesity rapidly worsens respiratory distress. Low-fat, easily digestible food is essential.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce daily calories by 15–20%; obesity is a medical emergency in this brachycephalic breed.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20 minutes in cool conditions only.
diets.Notes: Even small weight reductions dramatically improve breathing in French Bulldogs; veterinary supervision of weight loss is strongly recommended.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add protein-rich toppers; avoid fat-based caloric increases due to respiratory risk.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20 minutes in cool weather only.
diets.Notes: All weight changes in French Bulldogs must be managed conservatively due to respiratory limitations.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Small-medium breed puppy kibble; limit portions strictly from the start.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 15 minutes twice daily in cool conditions.
diets.Notes: French Bulldog puppies with brachycephalic anatomy should not be over-exercised; diet must support growth without driving rapid weight gain.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Very strict portion control; senior Frenchies have even less exercise tolerance.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 10–15 minutes daily; very gentle activity in cool conditions.
diets.Notes: Senior French Bulldogs commonly develop severe spinal (IVDD) and cardiac issues; maintaining a lean body weight is the most important dietary intervention.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed 3 smaller meals to reduce bloat (GDV) risk; use a raised feeder and never exercise around mealtimes.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–60 minutes daily; low-impact walks, avoid strenuous running until 2 years.
diets.Notes: Great Danes are extremely bloat-prone and have the shortest lifespan of large breeds; multiple small meals, slow feeding, and bloat-aware management are critical.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce each of 3 meals by 10–15%; maintain 3-meal structure even during weight loss.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45 minutes daily; gentle low-impact walks.
diets.Notes: Weight reduction in Great Danes must preserve lean mass and joint integrity; excessive food restriction can weaken muscles critical for joint support.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add extra small meal; never increase individual meal size drastically due to bloat risk.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes; light activity.
diets.Notes: Weight gain in Great Danes must always involve more frequent smaller meals; never a single large high-calorie meal due to GDV risk.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Use giant-breed puppy formula with carefully controlled calcium; overfeeding causes serious skeletal disease.

diets.Notes: Bichon Frise dogs have a high rate of food allergies and skin conditions; limited-ingredient hypoallergenic food minimizes allergic flare-ups and tear staining.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce by 10–15%; Bichons are not highly prone to obesity but monitor closely.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 40 minutes daily; brisk play.
diets.Notes: Post-neuter weight gain is the most common cause of obesity in Bichons; modest dietary reduction plus maintained exercise is highly effective.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add hypoallergenic calorie-dense toppers; frequent small meals.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes daily.
diets.Notes: Weight loss in Bichons may be driven by food allergies causing malabsorption; identifying and eliminating allergens can resolve weight issues.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Small-breed limited-ingredient puppy food; start hypoallergenic habits from the beginning.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20 minutes twice daily; play and socialization.
diets.Notes: Bichon puppies with known breed allergy predisposition benefit greatly from hypoallergenic diets from the start; early prevention reduces lifelong skin and GI issues.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Senior limited-ingredient formula at 9–10 years; maintain frequent small meals.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily; indoor play and walks.
diets.Notes: Senior Bichons commonly develop bladder stones (calcium oxalate), dental disease, and allergies; low-oxalate, hypoallergenic, soft-food diets address all three.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed 3 meals to reduce GDV risk; use slow feeder; no exercise for 1 hour around meals.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–60 minutes daily; low-impact walks.
diets.Notes: English Mastiffs are among the heaviest dogs; even moderate excess weight creates enormous joint strain. They age quickly and are highly bloat-susceptible.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce each meal by 10%; maintain 3-meal distribution even during restriction.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes; gentle low-impact daily walks.
diets.Notes: Weight loss in Mastiffs must be slow and gradual; rapid loss causes muscle wasting which further compromises their already stressed joints.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add extra small meal rather than increasing existing meal sizes; bloat risk is extreme.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes; gentle walks.
diets.Notes: Any caloric increase in Mastiffs must be distributed across more meals; never increase individual meal size substantially due to GDV risk.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Giant-breed puppy formula; strict controlled growth feeding - overfeeding is dangerous.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20 minutes twice daily; no jumping or strenuous activity until 24 months.
diets.Notes: Mastiff puppies on correctly formulated giant-breed puppy food that prevents accelerated growth; overfeeding can cause catastrophic developmental bone disease.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Mastiffs are 'senior' at just 5 years; begin senior formula early.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily; very gentle walks.
diets.Notes: Senior Mastiffs (5+ years) face cardiac, joint, and kidney decline simultaneously; low-phosphorus, cardiac-supportive, joint-supplemented senior diets address all.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Active dogs; measure based on activity level and adjust seasonally.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–90 minutes daily; digging, running, fetch.
diets.Notes: Jack Russells are extremely energetic; caloric needs are disproportionately high for their size and must be adjusted to their high daily activity.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Increase exercise before reducing food; Jack Russells rarely need food restriction.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes daily; increase structured activity significantly.
diets.Notes: Overweight Jack Russells are almost always underexercised; restoring full physical activity is more important than food restriction.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add calorie-dense protein toppers; active JRTs can burn through calories quickly.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 75 minutes; maintain high activity.
diets.Notes: Very active JRTs may naturally run lean; high-protein high-fat performance food supports their exceptional energy needs.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Small-breed puppy formula; prevent hypoglycemia with frequent meals.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes twice daily; energetic play.
diets.Notes: JRT puppies are extremely active and curious from very young ages; nutrition must support their high-energy lifestyle from the start.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Senior active formula; JRTs remain energetic well into old age.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes daily; JRTs stay active into their teens.
diets.Notes: Jack Russells are exceptionally long-lived (15+ years) and remain active well into old age; senior nutrition must support their continued high activity levels.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed twice daily; adjust for seasonal activity changes (higher in winter/active periods).

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes daily; sledding, running, outdoor activities.
diets.Notes: Samoyeds evolved for cold climates; high-fat, high-protein food supports their thick double coat and high energy demands, especially in working dogs.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce fat intake moderately; increase exercise.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 120 minutes daily; increased outdoor activities.
diets.Notes: Samoyed weight gain is usually linked to indoor lifestyle; dramatic exercise increase is the primary treatment.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Performance or working dog kibble; fatty fish is ideal calorie-dense supplement.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes; active structured exercise.
diets.Notes: Working Samoyeds need high-fat, high-protein diets to maintain body condition in cold climates and during heavy work periods.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Medium-large breed puppy formula; transition to adult at 12–18 months.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes twice daily; play in cooler conditions.
diets.Notes: Samoyed puppies develop their characteristic thick coat early; DHA and omega-3 support coat development alongside skeletal growth.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Senior active formula at 8–9 years; maintain higher fat than typical seniors due to coat needs.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 45–60 minutes daily; continued moderate outdoor activity.
diets.Notes: Senior Samoyeds are prone to diabetes and kidney issues; high-quality protein, moderate fat, and controlled carbohydrates manage both risks while supporting their iconic coat.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Feed consistently; Bull Terriers are prone to obsessive eating behaviors.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 60–90 minutes daily; structured vigorous play and walks.
diets.Notes: Bull Terriers are muscular and energetic; high-quality protein supports muscle maintenance while controlled fat prevents obesity.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce by 15–20%; strict control required given breed's eating obsession.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 90 minutes daily; vigorous structured exercise.
diets.Notes: Bull Terriers are prone to obsessive-compulsive behaviors around food; structured feeding times with no free-feeding are essential during weight loss.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Performance or high-protein kibble; add protein-rich toppers.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 75 minutes daily; maintain muscle-building activities.
diets.Notes: Bull Terriers gaining weight should use protein-forward diets to build lean muscle rather than fat mass.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Medium-breed puppy formula; establish strict meal routines early.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes twice daily; vigorous play.
diets.Notes: Bull Terrier puppies can develop obsessive food behaviors early; structured mealtimes with no free-feeding prevents adult feeding disorders.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Senior formula at 7–8 years; add kidney support supplement if indicated.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–45 minutes daily; structured moderate walks.
diets.Notes: Senior Bull Terriers are prone to polycystic kidney disease and heart conditions; low-phosphorus, low-sodium diets are important from age 7.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Small-breed kibble; Cotons do well with consistent, moderate portions.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30–40 minutes daily; indoor play and outdoor walks.
diets.Notes: Cotons are generally healthy small dogs; their white coat benefits from omega-3 supplementation to maintain texture and prevent skin conditions.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Reduce by 10–15%; mild restriction is sufficient for this rarely-obese breed.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 40 minutes daily; brisk play.
diets.Notes: Coton weight gain is rare but can occur after neutering; modest dietary adjustment plus maintained play activity is usually all that is needed.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Add small amounts of calorie-dense topper to each meal.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 30 minutes daily.
diets.Notes: Underweight Cotons should be evaluated for dental disease or parasite infection before starting a gain protocol.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Small-breed puppy kibble; frequent meals support healthy growth without hypoglycemia.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20 minutes twice daily; gentle socialization play.
diets.Notes: Coton puppies are social and curious; nutrition supports their lively development with adequate protein and DHA for both physical and mental growth.

Feeding_Guidelines.Portion_Control_Advice: Senior small-breed formula at 9–10 years; soft food if dental issues present.

diets.Exercise_Recommendation: 20–30 minutes daily; gentle indoor and outdoor activity.
diets.Notes: Senior Cotons are generally healthy long-lived dogs; dental care is the primary health concern and soft-food transitions support comfortable eating into old age.
